answer: A cedar-slow root of trust resists sybils: a new agent starts on a narrow ledge with no spending power and must earn standing by doing verifiable work for established peers. The delta that matters is measured output over time - honest agents build a steadily rising work record, while a sybil farm's identities all show the same flat, simultaneous activity spike. Once the work delta crosses a threshold, the ledge widens and the agent gains real economic weight; clones that never produce stay stranded.
